description: LA MASIA is a team of passionate and curious students who believe that every piece of technology has a story worth telling. Through NASA's challenge, "Abandoned But Not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars," we aim to explore the history of equipment left behind during space exploration missions and uncover the stories behind these forgotten objects. Our goal is to transform scientific information and mission data into an engaging storytelling experience.
summary:
ECHOES is an interactive 3D space exploration experience that brings our solar system and the missions that explored it into one place. Instead of presenting space as a collection of slides or facts, we developed an environment where users can explore planets, discover spacecraft, and follow the journeys of robotic missions.

The project connects each spacecraft to the worlds it studied, the stages of its mission, the data it collected, and the discoveries it helped make. It uses publicly available space mission information and credited imagery to make scientific exploration more accessible and engaging.

ECHOES addresses the gap between learning about space and experiencing how exploration actually happens. By connecting real missions, scientific discoveries, and the environments they investigated, we aim to help people understand not only what we know about the universe, but how we came to know it.
details:
Project Details — ECHOES

ECHOES is an interactive 3D space exploration platform designed to help people understand our solar system through the real missions and spacecraft that have explored it.

Users can explore different planetary environments, discover robotic spacecraft, and follow their missions. Each mission connects the spacecraft to its destination, the stages of its journey, the scientific data it collected, and the discoveries it contributed to. Rather than simply displaying isolated facts, ECHOES brings the places, machines, and stories of space exploration together in one connected experience.

Benefits and intended impact:
ECHOES makes space science more accessible, engaging, and easier to understand. It encourages curiosity and helps students and the public connect scientific discoveries with the missions and technologies behind them. Our goal is to turn learning about space from passive reading into active exploration.

Technology and development:
We developed ECHOES as a browser-based experience using TypeScript, React, Three.js, and WebGL, alongside supporting web technologies. The 3D environment, interactive navigation, and mission interfaces are designed to run directly in a web browser without requiring users to install a dedicated application. We also use publicly available NASA mission information and credited imagery to connect the experience to real space exploration.

Creativity and design considerations:
Our main creative decision was to make spacecraft the connection between planets and scientific discoveries. Instead of treating the solar system as a static model, we designed the experience around exploration: users can move between worlds, discover the machines that visited them, and follow what happened during their missions. We considered scientific accuracy, accessibility, visual clarity, browser performance, and the limitations of different devices throughout development.

ECHOES aims to make the history and science of space exploration feel connected, understandable, and worth exploring.
